challenge.objective: Make starting a Journey feel desirable and safe for a normal user — pull them off the comfortable Highlights/Stories default and get them to publicly document something unfinished. Reach is the easy part when you own Instagram.

truths.title: The enemy is a default, not a competitor
truths.text: People already document progress through Stories and group it in Highlights. Marketing has to reframe that habit as the first rung of something better — not fight it.

truths.title: The barrier is emotional, not functional
truths.text: Posting ‘day one, I’m bad at this’ cuts against Instagram’s curated, aspirational culture. The central job is to make beginning — visibly, imperfectly — feel brave and aspirational rather than embarrassing.

positioning.one_liner: Stories show what’s happening today. Your profile shows who you are. Journeys show who you’re becoming.
positioning.promise: Get recognized for what you’re working toward — not just what you’ve already achieved. Journeys turns your progress into something people can follow, cheer, and find.
positioning.wont_say: “A better way to group your content by theme.” That framing loses to Highlights on simplicity and misses the point. We sell distribution, progress, guidance, and being seen — never organization.

pillars.name: Progress, not perfection
pillars.truth: Your grid is your highlight reel; your Journey is the real story.
pillars.motivation: Speaks to authenticity-fatigue and removes the curation-anxiety barrier.

pillars.name: You don’t have to figure it out alone
pillars.truth: Meta AI helps you find the next step — creators, communities, the right gear, what to do at your stage.
pillars.motivation: Speaks to the inspiration-to-action problem that sends people off-platform.

pillars.name: Someone’s rooting for you
pillars.truth: Followers can follow along, cheer each update, and celebrate the finish.
pillars.motivation: Speaks to social motivation and accountability — the thing that makes progress stick.

hero.name: Everyone Starts at Day One
hero.concept: Pair people’s polished, impressive ‘now’ with their humble, awkward beginning. The truth it lands: everything impressive started somewhere unglamorous — and that somewhere is worth sharing.
hero.why: It reframes the exact thing people fear (posting imperfect beginnings) as the most relatable, aspirational, human thing they can do — and implicitly contrasts a living Journey against the static, perfected grid. It’s endlessly extensible across every category.

personas.day_one: Couldn’t run a single mile without stopping to walk.
personas.now: Crossing the finish line at mile 26.2.
A gallery-worthy shot people stop to look at.

personas.day_one: A messy first prototype held together with tape.
Fumbling through five words of a new language.

waves.theme: High-accountability, clear milestones, already share publicly

founding.what: Recruit a curated cohort of creators across every beachhead category to begin a real Journey publicly, from scratch, at launch — documented honestly, day one included. Their Journeys become the reference for ‘what good looks like’ and the first thing new users see.
founding.ask: Not an ad read — genuine participation: start a real Journey, post on your real cadence, and invite your audience to follow along. Authenticity is the asset; a polished sponsored post would undercut the whole ‘progress not perfection’ message.
founding.incentive: Amplification. Instagram actively pushes Founding Journeys to interest-matched audiences beyond the creator’s own followers — costs nothing Meta isn’t already doing, is a stronger pull than a flat fee, self-selects for consistent posters, and directly seeds the discovery the launch depends on.
jobs: Sets the cultural default: honest, in-progress, imperfect is celebrated.
Turns each creator’s community into a ready-made, interest-matched on-ramp that avoids the void.

tiers.role: A few big names for the cultural moment & PR
Broad across niches for category penetration
‘Anyone can be a founding member’ so it never feels closed

Owned.note: Meta’s own surfaces — the biggest advantage, and the COMPLETE launch set. Note: NO Reels entry point of any kind; that is a later-phase move the roadmap must earn first.
items: Lifecycle nudges — only within a specific beachhead community

Earned.note: The cultural moment — a story about authenticity and the end of the perfect grid, not a feature announcement.
items: PR around the ‘Day One’ idea & the Founding Journeys cohort
Creator-led organic reach as the cohort invites their communities
Completed-Journey recaps as inherently shareable earned media

Paid.note: Tightly targeted — not a broad awareness buy.
items: Targeted to high-intent signals (repeat category-Reels watchers)
Retargeting completed-Journey recaps as proof-driven recruitment

sequence.move: Seed quietly — recruit & onboard the Founding Journeys cohort; build a body of exemplary content in the closed beta before the public arrives.
‘Everyone Starts at Day One’ goes live with the cohort’s public Journeys and the Highlight-conversion prompt. Splash concentrated on Wave 1 categories.
Roll out Wave 2 & Wave 3 creator campaigns category by category; surface the first completed Journeys as proof and as the next wave of creative.
Completed-Journey recaps become the self-renewing marketing asset; each new surface (WhatsApp, Reels, Facebook, Glasses) gets a category-matched creator push, not a generic relaunch.

measurement.items: Campaign reach, brand-lift on the core message, earned-media volume & sentiment.
Campaign-attributable Journey starts; Highlight → Journey conversion rate.
Follower → follow-along conversion from creator audiences; share of new Journeys from creator campaigns vs organic discovery.

Do campaign-sourced Journey-starters hit the north-star (a 3rd update within 30 days, by follower segment)? If acquired users don’t retain, the format isn’t ready to advertise harder — fix the product before spending more on reach.

risks.detail: Over-indexing on ‘go viral’ attracts performers and pushes the culture back toward the polished grid Journeys was meant to escape. Always frame recognition as being seen for showing up — never follower growth.
Don’t promise discovery the product can’t yet deliver for small accounts. Marketing and the discovery engine have to ship in lockstep.
Never message Journeys as ‘organize your content.’ Lead with progress, guidance, and being seen — the things Highlights structurally cannot do.
A slick ad for ‘post your imperfect beginnings’ is self-defeating; the creative must feel as human as the behavior it asks for.
